Archaeology courses in India: BA, MA, diploma and PhD routes

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

Most archaeologists in India take a BA in history or a related subject, then an MA in archaeology or in ancient Indian history, culture and archaeology. Key institutions include Deccan College in Pune and the ASI's Institute of Archaeology at Greater Noida, which offers a postgraduate diploma, alongside university departments such as those at BHU, MSU Baroda and Calcutta.

Talaash Heritage runs career sessions on archaeology courses for students and parents, plus admissions and research clinics, online or at your school or college.

Start with a career session, not a brochure

Students often arrive at archaeology through a museum visit, a documentary or a history teacher, and then find course information scattered and confusing. Before choosing a college, it helps to understand how the routes fit together and what each leads to.

Our session on archaeology after Class 12 is built for exactly that moment, for students and parents together. For those already in college, BA to MA archaeology pathways maps the options for postgraduate study, and the MA admissions and portfolio clinic helps with entrance preparation and applications.

Archaeology after Class 12: the undergraduate stage

Very few Indian universities offer a BA in archaeology alone. The usual first degree is a BA in history, ideally with ancient Indian history, or in a related subject such as anthropology, geography or Sanskrit. Some universities offer a BA in ancient Indian history, culture and archaeology, often shortened to AIHC.

Science students are not shut out. Geology, botany, zoology, chemistry and computer science graduates are valuable in archaeological science, remote sensing, archaeobotany and archaeozoology, and some MA programmes admit graduates from any discipline. Humanities students should pick subjects that build reading, writing and a sense of chronology; Sanskrit or another classical language is a strong addition.

MA in archaeology: the main specialist degree

The MA is where most Indian archaeologists receive their real training. Courses cover prehistory, protohistory, historical archaeology, field methods, epigraphy, numismatics, art and architecture, and often a compulsory excavation or field training component. Admission is usually through a university entrance test or the national CUET-PG, depending on the university.

Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in Pune, a deemed university, is one of India's oldest centres of archaeological research and training, with a long record of excavations and an MA in archaeology. Several central and state universities also have established departments, including Banaras Hindu University, Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, the University of Calcutta, the University of Delhi and the University of Kerala. Programme names vary: look for archaeology, AIHC or ancient history and archaeology.

Institute of Archaeology, Greater Noida: the ASI's training school

The Archaeological Survey of India runs its own training institute, the Institute of Archaeology, now named after Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya and located at Greater Noida. It offers a two-year Postgraduate Diploma in Archaeology for students who already hold a master's degree in a relevant subject, with training in excavation, exploration, conservation, epigraphy, numismatics and museology, and close contact with ASI work.

Admission is competitive and based on an entrance examination and interview announced by the ASI. Because eligibility rules and schedules can change, check the ASI website for the current notice before applying.

Diplomas, certificate courses and short courses

Many universities, museums and institutes offer certificate or diploma courses in museology, conservation, epigraphy, numismatics and art history, often part-time. These suit working people, teachers and those testing their interest before a full degree. The National Museum Institute in New Delhi, a deemed university, offers postgraduate degrees in art history, conservation and museology, closely related to archaeology.

Short skills courses are also useful during a degree. Learning to read Brahmi, draw pottery or record a site makes a student stand out on an excavation. Courses such as our Brahmi workshop or site mapping and measured drawing fit around university study.

PhD and research in archaeology

A PhD is essential for academic posts and helpful for senior research positions. Most universities with MA programmes also supervise doctoral research, and admission typically requires UGC-NET or an equivalent qualification plus a research proposal. Choosing a topic and supervisor is the hardest step; our PhD research direction clinic and research proposal lab help with both.

Some students go abroad for postgraduate study, especially in archaeological science. Our guide to how to become an archaeologist in India explains where each qualification can lead.

Questions people ask

Can I study archaeology after Class 12?

Yes. Most students take a BA in history, ancient Indian history, culture and archaeology, anthropology or a related subject, then specialise with an MA in archaeology. A few universities offer archaeology papers or programmes at undergraduate level. Students from science streams can also enter through MA programmes that accept all disciplines.

Which is the best institute for archaeology in India?

There is no single best institute; it depends on your interests. Deccan College in Pune has one of the longest records in archaeological research and fieldwork. The ASI's Institute of Archaeology at Greater Noida offers practical postgraduate training. University departments such as those at BHU, MSU Baroda and Calcutta each have their own strengths.

Is a science background useful for archaeology?

Very useful. Archaeology increasingly relies on scientific methods such as dating, isotope analysis, ancient DNA, archaeobotany, archaeozoology, geoarchaeology and remote sensing. Science graduates can specialise in these areas through MA and PhD programmes, often working alongside students from history backgrounds.

What is the PG Diploma in Archaeology from the Institute of Archaeology?

It is a two-year postgraduate diploma run by the Archaeological Survey of India's Institute of Archaeology at Greater Noida. It takes students who already have a relevant master's degree and gives practical training in excavation, conservation, epigraphy, numismatics and museology. Check the ASI website for current eligibility and admission notices.

Can I study archaeology online in India?

Full degrees in archaeology need fieldwork, so they are mostly taught in person. Distance programmes in history or related subjects exist, and many short courses in epigraphy, numismatics, heritage and archaeology are available online. These are a good way to build knowledge alongside a degree or job.

Do I need Sanskrit to study archaeology?

Sanskrit is not essential for most archaeology programmes, but it helps greatly in historical archaeology, epigraphy and art history. Learning Brahmi and some Prakrit or Sanskrit makes it possible to read inscriptions directly. Prehistory and archaeological science need it far less.
